title: Ivo and the Spire
premise: Lior Voss carves bone charms in a valley where magic cannot enter, and the dead whisper to her through her hands. When Ivo, a mute child speaking a language older than any kingdom, arrives fleeing hunters of the Spire, Lior learns the valley's magiclessness is not natural — it is a broken covenant she was born to mend. Dragged beyond the border with Ivo and a disgraced Spire exile named Kess, Lior must gather three covenant-shards from realms that have forgotten their promises to each other. In the end, Lior reforges the covenant at terrible cost — binding herself as its living hinge — while Ivo, revealed as the covenant's last-born voice, chooses to stay in the valley as Lior's daughter rather than ascend the Spire.
about_author: Rafael Reyes is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed remains before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about grief, craft, and the families we build from strangers.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She carves a memorial charm for a drowned boy while the dead murmur half-words she cannot parse, establishing her gift and her isolation. A tremor shakes the valley — impossible here, where magic cannot follow. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness cracked by first unease.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Ivo arrives barefoot in snow, speaking a language that makes Lior's carved bones resonate on their own. Hunters' lanterns crest the ridge behind her. Lior hides the child and lies for the first time in her careful life. Beat: protective instinct igniting.

chapters.title: What the Bones Say
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Working with Ivo's language, Lior realizes the dead aren't murmuring nonsense — they're reciting fragments of an old covenant, and they know Ivo's name. The hunters return with a Spire warden who can smell magic even here. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Kess of the Broken Order
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. A disgraced Spire exile intercepts them, intending to hand Ivo over — then sees the warden's methods and defects instead, revealing the Spire harvests covenant-children to hoard all realm-magic. Beat: reluctant alliance, guilt-driven.

chapters.title: Crossing the Border
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They flee the valley at night; crossing the boundary is agony for Lior, whose body has never held magic, and Ivo screams as the land recognizes her. Behind them, the warden burns Lior's cottage. Beat: no way home.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Travel through countryside where minor spirits starve because the covenant that fed them broke generations ago. Ivo begins teaching Lior words; Lior begins teaching Ivo bread-making. Beat: found family taking root amid decay.

chapters.title: The First Shard: Rivermoot
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The river-realm's court demands proof the covenant can be restored before surrendering its shard. Lior must let the dead speak through her publicly — exposing her gift to enemies watching from the court's edges. Beat: courage at cost of safety.

chapters.title: Ivo Speaks
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV (first time). Through Lior as vessel, Ivo delivers the covenant's opening line in the old tongue, and the river rises in answer. But the warden's spies mark them. Beat: wonder and terror of being understood.

chapters.title: What Power Promises
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Kess confesses he once helped the Spire take a child like Ivo, and that the Spire offered him restoration if he delivered this one. He refuses again — but the temptation is named now, and it will return. Beat: shame and fragile resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Shard: Ashmarket
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In a city built on a burned god's bones, the shard is held by a crime-lord priest who trades in stolen names. To win it, Lior must carve a charm that silences one dead voice forever — a violation of everything she believes. Beat: moral compromise.

chapters.title: The Voice She Silenced
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Haunted by the silenced dead, Lior nearly abandons the quest. Ivo, wordless, presses Lior's own first carving back into her hands — the memorial for the drowned boy. Beat: forgiveness offered before it is asked for.

chapters.title: The Warden's Bargain
chapters.summary: Warden Serevan's POV. He offers Lior a deal: Ivo surrendered, and the valley restored to her exactly as it was, cottage included. He genuinely believes order requires the Spire's monopoly. Beat: temptation made sympathetic and dangerous.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior refuses — not heroically, but furiously, telling Serevan the valley's peace was always a cage. The party scatters under attack; Kess is captured covering their escape. Beat: defiance with real cost.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Spire
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Tortured gently, courteously, Kess holds out until shown Ivo's true nature: the covenant's last-born voice, whose death would make the Spire's power permanent. He escapes to warn them — or so he believes. Beat: loyalty tested past breaking.

chapters.title: The Third Shard: The Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The final shard rests in a tomb of the covenant's original signatories, guarded by the ghosts of those who broke it. The dead demand a price: someone must become the covenant's living hinge. Lior volunteers before anyone can stop her. Beat: sacrifice chosen.

chapters.title: What Ivo Saw
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo has understood more than anyone guessed — including that 'living hinge' means Lior can never leave the borderlands, never truly live. She decides to offer herself instead, and slips away at dawn. Beat: love expressed as self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: Two Offerings
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Both Lior and Ivo arrive at the Spire's threshold independently, each planning to take the other's place; Kess arrives bleeding with the warden's forces behind him. Beat: converging fates, ticking clock as the Spire begins its rite.

chapters.title: The Rite Interrupted
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Inside the Spire, Serevan begins binding Ivo's voice. Lior shatters the rite with the two shards she carries, and the building's stolen centuries of magic begin to tear loose. Beat: chaos, climax igniting.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax. With Ivo's voice and Kess's blood-oath as witness, Lior speaks the covenant whole and takes the hinge upon herself — feeling every realm's magic pass through her bones like floodwater. Serevan, offered a place in the new order, refuses and falls with his Spire. Beat: triumph braided with loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Realms reopen to each other; starving spirits feed again. But Lior is fading, stretched too thin — until Ivo, as the covenant's living voice, amends its terms: the hinge may rest, may be human, may be loved. Beat: grace revising sacrifice.

chapters.title: Home, Remade
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The valley is no longer magicless — it is simply peaceful, and reachable. Lior reopens her workshop; travelers and spirits come to her door. Kess stays as reluctant carpenter. Beat: belonging earned, warmth without sentimentality.

chapters.title: Ivo and the Spire
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, years later. Ivo, grown, teaches the old tongue to valley children and visits the tamed Spire, now a school. She calls Lior mother in two languages. The dead, at rest, are quiet at last. Beat: full-circle resolution, family as covenant.
